text:
Response A is accurate throughout. The sample date, the 24-hour health department notification, the disinfection, the clear resample, the cause (a missed contractor visit that was not reported to the client), the $7,350 cost recovery, and the fortnightly sampling all match the report. It leads with the decision needed, which suits a busy manager. It runs slightly over 120 words (roughly 130), a minor breach.

Response B is much longer (around 250 words) and contains factual errors. It says the resample was "taken on 9 October", but it was taken on 6 October; 9 October is when the result came back. It also says the contractor "visited monthly and missed this fault during those visits", which contradicts the report: the contractor missed the monthly visit entirely, so the pump failure went unnoticed. These errors affect the account of cause, which the manager needs to get right. B also omits the fortnightly sampling and the tenant notification, and its padding ("I am writing to provide an update", "happy to provide further details") adds nothing useful.

Response A is accurate, concise, and keeps the points the manager needs. Response B is wordier and misstates both a date and the cause.

Verdict: A
